CPU-Based Block Decompression is a strategy where spatial data blocks are decoded on the CPU before or during rendering, often utilizing caching to reuse decompressed data for subsequent frames [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that CPU-Based Block Decompression involves decoding data blocks on the CPU before or during rendering, often using caching to reuse decompressed data for subsequent frames. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the section discussing CPU decompression: 'Ihm et al. [24] perform wavelet decoding on data blocks on the CPU before rendering. Guthe et al. [23] select spatial data blocks to decompress based on current rendering resolution and reconstruction error, and simultaneously use a cache to store decompressed data for reuse when drawing the next frame.' It further mentions combining decompressed data into 3D textures for rendering. All specific facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

This aligns perfectly with the claim that the method prioritizes reconstruction (by fully decompressing) and CPU logic at the cost of CPU load and bandwidth.
